section: Science · Ch41 — Matter, Materials & Natural Resources
subject: Science
stem: When ice is heated and turns into water, and the water is further heated to become steam, the process shows that matter can:

options.option_text: Change its physical state (solid to liquid to gas) with heat, without changing its chemical identity
Be destroyed entirely and cease to exist
Change into a completely different chemical substance
Only exist in the solid state under normal conditions

explanation: Melting and boiling are physical changes — the substance (H₂O) remains chemically the same across solid, liquid and gas states; only the arrangement/energy of particles changes.

section: Science · Ch41 — Matter, Materials & Natural Resources
subject: Science
stem: To separate a mixture of sand and salt dissolved in water, the correct sequence of methods is:

options.option_text: Filtration (to remove sand) followed by evaporation (to recover salt from water)
Evaporation alone, without any filtration
Filtration alone, without any evaporation
Magnetic separation only

explanation: Sand (insoluble) is removed first by filtration; the salt remains dissolved in the filtrate, from which it is recovered by evaporating the water. Magnetic separation only works for magnetic materials like iron filings.

section: Science · Ch41 — Matter, Materials & Natural Resources
subject: Science
stem: Solar energy, wind energy and hydro-power are classified as renewable resources mainly because they:

options.option_text: Naturally replenish continuously and do not get depleted with use
Are manufactured in factories
Take millions of years to form
Are found only underground

explanation: Renewable resources replenish naturally on a human timescale (sunlight, wind, flowing water), unlike fossil fuels which take millions of years to form and are non-renewable.

section: Science · Ch41 — Matter, Materials & Natural Resources
subject: Science
stem: The type of soil found in the Krishna-Godavari delta region of Andhra Pradesh, formed by river-deposited silt and highly fertile for paddy cultivation, is:

options.option_text: Alluvial soil
Black (regur) soil
Red soil
Laterite soil

explanation: Alluvial soil, deposited by rivers like the Krishna and Godavari, is rich in nutrients and ideal for paddy — hence the deltas are called the 'rice bowl' of Andhra Pradesh. Black soil is typical of the Deccan (cotton-growing) plateau.

section: Science · Ch41 — Matter, Materials & Natural Resources
subject: Science
stem: Which property is generally true of metals but NOT of non-metals?

options.option_text: Good conductivity of heat and electricity
Always exist as gases at room temperature
Always brittle and cannot be hammered into sheets
Never react with acids

explanation: Metals are typically good conductors of heat and electricity, malleable and ductile — unlike non-metals, which are generally poor conductors and often brittle in solid form (with exceptions like graphite).
